parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Iron(II) compounds are generally only stable in neutral, non-oxidising conditions.

It is difficult to determine the lattice energy of $\text{FeO}$ experimentally.
parts.text:
Use data from the *Data Booklet* and this Born-Haber cycle to calculate the lattice energy, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}$, of $\text{FeO}\text{(s)}$ in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Most naturally occurring samples of iron(II) oxide are found as the mineral wüstite.

Wüstite has formula $\text{Fe}_{20}\text{O}_{x}$. It contains both $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.

90% of the iron is present as $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and 10% is present as $\text{Fe}^{3+}$.

Deduce the value of $x$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State and explain how the lattice energy of $\text{FeO}\text{(s)}$ compares to the lattice energy of $\text{CaO}\text{(s)}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Heating of $\text{FeO}$ results in the formation of $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, as shown.

**reaction 1** $$4\text{FeO} \rightarrow \text{Fe} + \text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$$

Each formula unit of $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$ contains one $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and two $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.
parts.text: Show how reaction 1 can be described as a disproportionation reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem: $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4\text{(l)}$ can be electrolysed using inert electrodes to form Fe.
parts.text: Write the half-equation for the reaction that occurs at the anode during the electrolysis of $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4\text{(l)}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Calculate the maximum mass of iron metal formed when $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4\text{(l)}$ is electrolysed for six hours using a current of $50\text{ A}$.

Assume the one $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and two $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions are discharged at the same rate.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{LiFePO}_4$ can be used in lithium-ion rechargeable batteries.

When the cell is charging, lithium reacts with a graphite electrode to form $\text{LiC}_6$.

When the cell is discharging, the half-equations for the two processes that occur are as follows.

**anode half-equation** $\text{LiC}_6 \rightarrow 6\text{C} + \text{Li}^+ + \text{e}^-$

**cathode half-equation** $\text{Li}^+ + \text{FePO}_4 + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{LiFePO}_4$
parts.text: State one possible advantage of developing cells such as lithium-ion rechargeable batteries.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the cathode half-equation to determine the change, if any, in oxidation states of lithium and iron at the **cathode** during discharging.

| metal | change in oxidation state during discharging |  |

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Write the equation for the overall reaction that occurs when this cell is discharging.
